14 Quomodo inter se differant vox prolata & scripta?
Væ[?] sunt species generales vocis significatricis; una
prolata, altera scripta. Illæ autem inter se differunt
variis modis:
1. vox prolata natura seu origine prior est
scripta, sicut etiam loquela prior est ipsa scriptura.
2. vox
prolata semper est signum immediatum rei animo con-
ceptæ: vox vero scripta non item; cum sæpe rem animo
conceptam significet, mediante voce prolata.
3. vox
prolata est audibilis; scripta vero visibilis.
4. vox prola-
ta est transiens, scripta vero permanens.
5. vox prolata
maiorem vim ac ἐνέργειαν habet, ad imprimendum animo
rei signatæ conceptum, quam scripta.
6. vox prolata tan-
tum prodest præsentibus & audientibus; scripta vero et-
iam prodest absentibus & legentibus, adeoque toti po-
steritati.

page.notes: Page number 118 read at the head of the page; the last digit is slightly doubtful. The large initial of "Væ sunt" is hard to read, so the word is marked [?]. The first word of the left margin note "Quid sintit...endum" is doubtful. The Greek quotation from Aristotle (Topics II, 2) is not legible enough to transcribe letter by letter, so it is marked as illegible. The catchword "candis" is the start of the next word, "significandis". Where the printed text reads "quaeres", it is kept as printed.
